text:
Mark Scheifele has been the Jets' passer this season more than their finisher, and the finishing is the part that will come back. He has 18 points in 18 games, 14 of them assists, but only four goals on 7.3 expected (the quality of his chances). He's shooting 9.8% against a typical range for him of 13 to 18%. Goals tend to follow chances, and he keeps getting them.

He also scored the goal Winnipeg will remember from this stretch: a last-second power-play winner over Tampa Bay on Saturday, the third straight win after an eight-game skid. Over the skid itself he had zero points in five straight games, then nine in the last five. That's what a 33-year-old first-line center looks like when the bounces turn.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, which is why his assist totals hold up even in bad months. The worry, per Evolving-Hockey, is the other end: opponents got noticeably more chances with him on the ice in 2025-26 (bottom 3% of forwards). Our projection has him near 95 points.
